sources.transformation: Sample grain: month x measure (1996-01..2026-07 aggregate) and port x month x measure (2018+). Use measure = 'Personal Vehicle Passengers' as the leisure-relevant volume (plus 'Bus Passengers' and 'Pedestrians' as a labelled secondary); exclude Trucks, Trains. Quarterly `_full` = sum of the three months, guarded complete; `_m1` = first month only (Jul, the vintage observable today); `_m2` = first two months once Aug lands (~mid Oct); `_lag1`; y/y %. Port level: sum by state for a state split, or take Blaine/Peace Arch (WA) and Buffalo-Niagara (NY) as the two leisure corridors. Note the series counts ALL inbound persons at US ports (Canadians entering plus US residents returning), so it is corridor volume, not 'Canadians'; StatCan's Canadians-returning series is the mirror of the Canadian-resident half. Quarter key -> '3Q26' to join the panel. No FX, no seasonal adjustment (y/y).

sources.transformation: Wide UNWTO Compendium layout: semicolon-delimited, UTF-8 BOM, country header rows, indicator hierarchy across four unnamed columns, year columns 1995..2022 as strings with comma thousands separators, '..' = missing. Reshape: forward-fill country code/name down the block, concatenate the four indicator columns into one label, melt years to long (country, indicator, series flag TF/VF/TCE, year, value), parse numbers. Then take 2019 (pre-COVID structure) and 2022 (latest) origin-region shares per destination country, aggregate destination countries to Airbnb regions weighted by Airbnb regional nights shares (`*_nights_share_est_pct` columns of the regional panel), and write a 4x4 (origin region x destination region) share matrix plus country-level rows for the top 25 destinations. Annual only: no calendar alignment to quarters; used as a structural weight, never as a time series feature. No FX.

lanes.cross_source_notes: How the lane combines: daio is the only source here that can enter the V2/G2 walk-forward as a candidate EMEA feature (and it should be run once, in a new govdata_v2/ folder, with the pass line above); BTS is the US-side mirror of the StatCan Canada series the govdata survey already ranked (LIIA short-window survivor at 0.66, 24-10-0053 duplicate), so it belongs in the NA lap exhibit, not the nowcast; UNWTO supplies the structural origin x destination weights for WP-X; Dubai carries nothing usable. Together they give WP-X one destination-volume series per region that is current (daio for EMEA, StatCan/BTS for the Canada->NA corridor, held ANAC/IBGE for LatAm, held JNTO/ABS for APAC) and an annual O-D prior to weight them. What other lanes should know: (1) the Canada corridor is already held twice (data/processed/govdata/V/raw/statcan_liia_monthly.csv reaches Aug 2026 and its Sep lands ~10 Oct; data/processed/overnight/10_bench_canada_travel_monthly.csv is the 24-10-0053 monthly), so do not re-pull it a third time; (2) Eurostat avia_paoc is held but ragged (EU27 ends 2025-12), so daio is the European air-volume series to use, and its git history is a free vintage record; (3) daio's EMEA read today is +3.0% flt_da QTD vs +1.2% in 2Q26 and +3.2% in 1Q26, a mild re-acceleration in flights that is directionally consistent with the 2Q26 letter's 'high-single digit, accelerating' EMEA phrase and gives no support to an EMEA deceleration story; flights vary 1-4 pp while nights vary 5-25 pp, so treat it as corroboration until the test says otherwise; (4) BTS confirms the NA base: US-Canada personal-vehicle passengers 3Q25 -23.2%, 4Q25 -21.5%, 1Q26 -8.4%, 2Q26 +12.0%, Jul 2026 +11.0%, so the 3Q26 and 4Q26 NA comps are arithmetic (the 'Canadians returning' feature is a lap, and it fades by 2Q27); (5) the regional targets in 10_regional_panel_quarterly.csv are letter buckets from 4Q24 (±1 pp) and derived residual intervals for 2Q23-3Q24 (±2 pp), which caps what any regional test can show on W1; (6) licence decisions needed from a human (WP-O): Eurocontrol reuse terms before committing daio CSVs or printing a number; Dubai DET terms if anyone wants the portal series; UNWTO is non-commercial with attribution and fine to cite; BTS is public domain. Nothing in this lane touches ADR, GBV, RNPL or the guide arithmetic, and nothing here should be proposed as a level input; the deliverable is one EMEA corroboration line and one NA exhibit before the 2 Oct memo.

lanes.cross_source_notes: How the lane combines: (1) Gap 20 (party size / LOS by destination country and year beside Airbnb's review-derived series): only the Booking.com accommodation-reviews panel carries guest_type + room_nights + accommodation_country + accommodation_type on one row, and it is already held in full (1,628,989 stays, data/raw/booking/rectour24_train_users.csv, processed by booking_party_composition.py). Its four guest_type classes map one-to-one onto the team's solo/couple/family/group composition with the same 1/2/3.9/4.7 weights, so the comparison is at country x year 2023 against the v2 Airbnb shards aggregated through market_geo.csv. It is one year (2023), review-filtered (>=3 topics, English), and the held 515k hotel set (2015-17) is hotels-only, so no Booking.com composition or LOS trend exists; everything is level and seasonal-profile corroboration, never a harness object. guest_type does NOT map to Airbnb 'seats' (Experiences/Services denominator units, -0.5pp); it maps to the unit-size chain (+0.63pp). (2) Cross-border share for WP-X: unrecoverable from every Booking.com release. accommodation-reviews anonymises guest_country into 135 tokens with zero overlap with accommodation_country; WSDM-2021 uses fictional countries; Bright Data has no guest origin. Do not de-anonymise tokens by modal inference without a human decision. WP-X must keep to NTTO / Eurostat / JNTO / INE / DATATUR and the reviewer-locale proxy already in its brief. (3) Gap 9 (competitor volumes): none of these gives a Booking.com alternative-accommodation volume series; the review sample's hotel 58% / apartment 8% / aparthotel 5% mix is a review-selection share, not inventory or nights share, so WS11's derived BKNG alt-accommodation nights (analysis/src/peer_readthrough/, branch krish/peer-readthrough) remains the only volume series. (4) Time series vs cross-section: accommodation-reviews = 2023 cross-section with check-in month; WSDM = Jan 2016-Feb 2017 reservations (one span, multi-city selection); Bright Data HF = six check-in dates Dec 2024-Feb 2025; Bright Data 1001 = one search, Jan 2025; the 'Buenos Aires' mirror = a real 2009-May 2023 review time series at a single 2023 vintage. (5) Licence: accommodation-reviews CC BY-SA 4.0 with a 'non-commercial' card sentence (already on disk and flagged in data/README.md; quoting is WP-O); WSDM CC BY-NC-ND plus Booking.com T&Cs (no derivatives, park); Bright Data = vendor MSA / no licence on scraped Booking.com pages (WP-O, park; consuming a vendor's scrape is the same class as running a scraper); the Inside Airbnb mirror is CC BY 4.0 Inside Airbnb, no new decision. (6) The one build in the lane is off-topic for gaps 9/20 but on-topic for the team's chain: the mis-titled HF mirror is a Mar-May 2023 vintage of the review store the stays-index survivor runs on, covering ~106 of the 123 held markets plus the NYC pre-LL18 dump; it belongs with WP-K (Theo) and the E scripts, and its pre-registered test can corroborate or downgrade the reviews index's W1 claim before the 26 Sep card freeze. sources.transformation: Sample grain: one row per (date = Sunday snapshot, act_symbol, period slot {Current Quarter, Next Quarter, Current Year, Next Year}, period_end_date) with consensus in whole USD, count, high, low, year_ago. To register grain: period = YYYYQn from period_end_date month for the two quarter slots (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec -> Q1..Q4) and FYyyyy for the two year slots (assert month == 12, ABNB FY = calendar year, same guard as consensus_history_loader.period_label); value = consensus / 1e6 -> musd; n_estimates = count; as_of_timestamp = snapshot date (the vintage, never the pull date); vendor = 'Zacks (via DoltHub post-no-preference/earnings)'; role = pit_history; pit_usable = True; vendor_attributed = True; url = the exact DoltHub SQL API query URL from manifest.json source_urls; source_path = data/processed/github_altdata/samples/dolthub-post-no-preference-earnings-consensus-vintages/sales_estimate_ABNB_BKNG_EXPE.csv; note = 'weekly Sunday snapshot; slot=<period>; high=<high/1e6>; low=<low/1e6>'; register_id = PIT-{period}-revenue-ZacksDolt-{YYYYMMDD}. Calendar alignment for guide dates: as-of join = latest snapshot with date < guide_date (strict, matching pit_consensus semantics); the 22 guide dates all resolve with lag 2-9 days (median 4). For prints: same rule with print_date. For WP-B revisions: value at the last Sunday <= d+30/60/90 minus value at the last Sunday < d, same period slot mapped by period_end_date (not by slot name, which rolls after each print). No FX or seasonal handling (USD, nominal levels). EPS rows (eps_estimate) are NOT appended until basis is reconciled: the sample's 2020Q4 EPS -9.19 vs the register's at_print eps_adj -8.4 shows the Zacks EPS basis differs from the press-quote adjusted basis.

Knowable before 5 Nov: yes, the 1 Nov 2026 snapshot will exist before the print and the 8 Nov snapshot after it (the DoltHub earnings_calendar does not yet list 5 Nov). Point-in-time: yes, each row is a dated snapshot and the Dolt commit history lets a human verify that historical rows were not back-edited (query dolt_log / AS OF on three sampled dates as a spot check). sources.test_and_pass_line: Tested against the existing register values and against the WP-A / WP-B pre-registered lines. T1 vendor-equivalence (pre-registered, run on the sample before any append): on the 18 pre_guide cells that carry a register value, median |Zacks-register|/register <= 1.0% AND sign(guide_mid - Street) agrees on >= 16/18 cells -> the DoltHub-Zacks series is 'corroboration / duplicate-grade' of the press-quote vendor and may fill the two holes (PG-2021Q4, PG-2024Q3) as a second-vendor fallback; on the 23 at_print cells median |diff| <= 0.5% (already observed 0.0%, max 1.79%). If T1 fails the series is a 'second vendor', not a fallback, and the holes stay open. lanes.cross_source_notes: How the lane combines. Two facts govern everything here. First, the harness (FORMAT 1.0) scores only targets 2021Q1..2026Q2 on fixed windows (W1 14 guide dates from 2023Q1, W2 10 from 2024Q1), and the driver history file data/processed/abnb_driver_history_quarterly.csv starts 2021Q1 with y/y from 2022Q1; quarterly nights levels exist publicly from 1Q19 (S-1) but y/y only from 1Q20, which is COVID. So no pre-2023 archive can add a scored quarter to any ABNB backtest; the answer to 'does it add scored quarters' is no, for every source in the lane. Second, the held 2025/2026 reviews dumps already contain review dates back to 2010 (index_quarterly.csv starts 1Q16), attrited about 15 percent per year; the pre-2023 archives therefore do not add history, they add un-attrited vintages of the same history. That is worth having for exactly one reason: the 0.68 stays-index result rests on the wedge being constant in time, and the archives let that be tested (the 2023 mirror on 2022-23, montera34 on 2016-19, ChicagoBooth and cs1951a at 7-11 year horizons). Seasonality (the partial-to-full quarter gap, currently n=3 years) can already be extended to 2016-2019 from the held 2026 dumps without any archive, because uniform per-listing attrition does not change within-year ratios; do that first, it is free. Priority order: (1) the 116-market Mar-May 2023 mirror, at least the 17-file 13-city subset (1.3 GB), saved under the E3 naming convention <market_key>_<dump_date>_reviews.csv.gz into the gitignored raw store, processed by copies of E3-E7 writing to a new data/processed/q3nowcast_v2/E/ folder (the E outputs are tracked data files; copy never overwrite), with the wedge-constancy test pre-registered at |delta| <= 2.0 pp global; (2) the NYC LL18 bracket from the mirror's NYC file, the Jan-2024 listings file and the held 2025-09-01 NYC dump, on a reviewed-active-listings basis, corroborating or disputing the CRA -56.1% that REG-01 leans on; (3) montera34 and ChicagoBooth reviews if time, for the attrition curve; (4) the cs1951a subset (Chicago, Austin, Nashville, SF, Boston, 2-2.5 GB) for the delta-reviews flow check and pre-2020 NA panel rows. Park tmasjc, the Zillow panel and treat Boston as an exhibit. Nothing here touches airbnb.com or needs a WP-O decision; every file is Inside Airbnb CC BY 4.0 under a mirror with no licence of its own, so cite Inside Airbnb with the dump date and never commit raw files (manifests with sha256 only). What other lanes should know: (a) the join key across all of these is the Inside Airbnb listing id, stable since 2015 (ids like 2595 appear in the 2015, 2023 and 2025 NYC files) and the market_key slug country_region_market; (b) the listing-count side of the NYC gap (dumps 2023-06-05, 2023-10-01, 2023-11-01, 2024-01-05, 2024-03-07) is still closed only by a human request through Inside Airbnb's data form, already recommended in the supply-panel note; the mirrors close the review side only; (c) the party-size pipeline can consume the mirror's files unchanged (full schema with comments), giving a 2023-vintage party-size point for the 13 cities, which the party-size lane may want; (d) if the v2 re-run changes any registered stays-index row it must be registered under a new method name and score.py re-run (WP-J); (e) none of this waits for 5 Nov and all of it fits before the 26 Sep card freeze if the mirror pull starts this week; total lane effort about 6 agent-days if everything is built, 2 days for the build_now rows.

lanes.cross_source_notes: Answer to the lane question, one line: none of the three libraries is needed. The cheapest route to (i) NCLH advance ticket sales, (ii) BKNG/EXPE deferred merchant bookings and (v) Form 4 is the keyless data.sec.gov companyconcept/companyfacts/submissions endpoints the repo already hits (capital_return_panel.py, abnb_eu_platform_and_backlog.py, bkng_head_to_head.py; cache data/raw/xbrl/<TICKER>.json, gitignored); the working tags are ContractWithCustomerLiabilityCurrent for NCLH/CCL/RCL (2017Q4+, pre-2018 tag to be checked for the E1 2015 start) and us-gaap:DeferredMerchantBookings for BKNG and EXPE (confirmed in the FSDS 2021q1 sample). Every value carries a filed date, so the vintage rule is 'earliest filed per period end'; the NCLH sample shows zero restatements >0.5% across 66 vintage rows, so first-filed equals final and the PIT panel is trivial. (iii) XBRL frames: pure duplicate of abnb_costlines_from_xbrl.py (which already does Q4 = FY - 9M); secfsdstools (7 GB, ABNB missing from 2021q1) and sec-data (drops filed dates, needs arelle) are parked; the crosswalk and full-index stitcher are duplicates of CIKs and dates already in the harness calendar and peer event log. (iv) 13F concentration: build from the SEC Form 13F structured data sets filtered on CUSIP 009066101 (22 quarters 2021q1-2026q2, ~1.5 agent-days), not from the Berkshire repo; fully point-in-time via FILING_DATE but the last point knowable before 5 Nov is the 30 Jun 2026 report, so it is an exhibit/cohort object for the capital-return and market-implied notes, never a KPI input. Form 4 is a half-day exhibit with a 2-day lag; both ownership objects get an optional pre-registered corroboration test against abnb_earnings_reactions.csv (|r| > 0.4 same sign on W1 and W2, permutation p < 0.10) and otherwise stay 'exhibit only'. A bonus fill for the inventory 7.2 wish-list 'period-end fully diluted share count' comes free from companyfacts (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding plus option and unvested-RSU counts). Transcript corpora: none adds an ABNB call (the team holds all 23); MAEC adds 24 peer excerpts 2015-2018 outside both windows; Lamini's full 49 MB file might hold 2019-2023 peer full calls but is unverified and copyrighted; ECTSum, Qin-Yang and FinBERT add nothing. All parked, consistent with the 948-test tone result. Harness caveat for the E1/E2 owners: targets.csv is ABNB-only, so NCLH and OTA kernels are scored locally with I0_protocol.walkforward and the note opens a harness change request; only the EXPE-as-ABNB-feature variant (lag 1, since EXPE's 10-Q files after ABNB's print) can be registered under a new method name for WP-C3. No source in this lane touches airbnb.com; the only ToS decisions are the iShares scraper (parked) and the Motley-Fool-derived transcript files (parked). Licences to flag if anything is ever redistributed: edgar-crawler and ECTSum GPL-3.0, MAEC CC BY-SA, trade-copier no licence (do not copy code).
